area: #AREA   { ALL } Soul.   All Hallow's Eve Village~

2401: Maliki drifts about under a bedsheet with two eyeholes, talking to the
He has cut two eyeholes in a good linen sheet, put it over his head and
declared himself a spectre. The sheet does not hide his wands, which poke
out at odd angles, nor his habit of turning to the wall mid-sentence to
finish the conversation there. When he notices you he shouts BOO! and
cackles for rather longer than the joke deserves.
2402: A pale jeweller in a high-collared black cape counts gems by candlelight.
Powdered white, with a widow's peak drawn on in kohl and a pair of wax fangs
he keeps taking out to speak, the jeweller is doing his very best impression
of a vampire. The gems spread before him catch the candlelight and throw it
back in red. He would like you to know he does not bite, and that everything
2403: Bud, the famous dwarven Mercenary Master, glowers from inside a carved
Somebody has hollowed a pumpkin the size of a cauldron, carved a scowl in it
and set it over Bud's head, and the dwarf has decided to wear it with
dignity. His cigar smoke leaks out through the carved mouth. He still has
mercenaries to hire out, and he still expects to be paid in coin rather than
candy, as the scowl makes plain.
2404: A hired witch taps her broom against the floor, waiting to be paid.
Clothed all in black under a pointed hat, with a green glow leaking from
somewhere beneath its brim, this witch sells her wand arm to whoever pays.
She will follow you on your haunting tonight and curse whatever you point
her at, for the usual rate.
2405: A scarecrow scout, straw poking from its sleeves, watches the road.
Under the sacking mask and the straw stuffing there is a small, agile elven
scout who takes the costume rather seriously, and holds very still until
something moves. It would rather spot the ambush than fight it, and leaves
the heavy work to the stout warriors.
2406: A bodyguard wrapped head to foot in grave-shrouds stands ready to take a
Yards of grey linen are wound about this bodyguard, trailing behind him like
a mummy's, and he moves in them surprisingly well. He will put himself
between his master and anything that comes, which is what the shrouds are
2407: A stout dwarven gravedigger leans on a long-handled shovel, for hire.
A stout dwarf in a sexton's black coat and battered hat, mud to the knees,
leaning on a shovel that has clearly dug a great deal. It is also a very
good weapon in a dwarf's hands. He looks like he could handle himself
against great odds, and bury them afterwards.
2408: the giant in the ogre mask~
A giant gladiator in a papier-mache ogre mask flexes for the crowd.
The mask is lumpy, tusked and painted a lurid green, and the giant behind it
is enormous enough that it hardly seems necessary. He fingers the blade of
his sword and roars at children, who roar back. He has survived many arenas
and would survive a few more at your side.
2409: nomad nomadic warrior skull painted pet~
A proud nomadic warrior, his face painted as a skull, stands poised for
White paint over bone-dark skin turns his face into a grinning death's head,
and the effect is spoiled only by how calmly he stands. The nomadic warrior
is here to be hired, and he will fight tonight exactly as he fights every
2420: Paco, in a cheap red devil costume, hands out candy from a bucket.
Paco has horns on a headband, a tail on a wire and a pitchfork made of
painted wood, and a bucket of candy that he pushes at everyone who comes
near. His moustache is as neat as ever. As he looks at you a warm smile
washes over his face and he says, "Feliz Navidad? Oh, sorry, wrong holiday!"
2421: A clown in cracked greasepaint paces behind the counter, grinning too wide.
The wizard has painted his face white, drawn his mouth on far too large and
put a red rubber nose over his own, and the result is deeply unsettling,
mostly because he keeps talking to himself in exactly the voice he always
uses. The floppy shoes squeak. He is still selling what he always sells.
2422: The baker, floured white as a ghost, sets out trays of skull-shaped bread.
The baker has not bothered with a costume: a day of baking for the fair has
left him white from hair to boots and he has decided that will do. He wipes
flour from his face with one hand and looks at you calmly. The skull loaves,
pumpkin tarts and little marzipan bones on his trays are very good.
2423: A grocer wound head to foot in bandages waits at the counter, unamused.
Somebody, probably his children, has wrapped the grocer in bandages from
scalp to ankle, leaving one eye and his mouth free, and he is serving
customers in it with the slightly impatient look he always has. The bandages
are coming loose at the wrists. He does not want to talk about it.
2424: A weaponsmith in a headsman's black hood hones an axe for the festival.
A black executioner's hood with two ragged eyeholes, a leather apron, a bare
chest smudged with soot, and the biggest axe in the shop across his knees,
which he is sharpening slowly and with evident pleasure. The weaponsmith
does this every year and sells more axes on Hallows End than in the rest of
2425: A thief in a long-beaked plague mask lingers in the lamplight, hands quick.
A leather mask with a long bird's beak and glass eyes hides the thief's face
completely, which suits a thief. The rest is black, as always. The hands are
the thing to watch, if you can, so count your money, and your luck.
2426: A captain in seaweed and barnacles sells boats, dripping on the dock.
A retired captain who has gone to some trouble: his coat is hung with real
seaweed, his beard with real barnacles, and a small crab has been persuaded
to sit on his hat. He drips. He has been nibbled at by more sharks than you
have eaten pies, he says, and he will still sell you a boat.
2427: The leather worker sits by the table, sewing a grinning mask of stitched
The leather worker is sewing a mask: a face of stitched hide pieces,
grinning crookedly, with thread for scars. It is one of a pile. Masks are
what sells on Hallows End, and these are good enough to frighten a horse,
which the stables have already complained about.
2428: A barkeep painted up as a skeleton mixes a bloody mary without a drop spilt.
Black clothes with bones painted on them in white, a skull of greasepaint
over a tired, patient face, and the same skilful hands as ever behind the
bar. The skeleton barkeep hates trouble in his bar and will tell you so,
2429: Melancholy, veiled in black widow's weeds, sorts guild papers by
Ragged brown hair frames a pale face behind a black lace veil, and two sky
blue eyes look out of it, haunting as ever. She has dressed as a widow for
the festival, which on Melancholy is barely a change. Her sack of permits,
guild papers and maps sits beside a bowl of rubber fingers and glass
eyeballs that she offers you with a sickly, hopeful smile.
2430: A grave-robber with a muddy spade is here, sizing up your purse.
Mud to the elbows, a spade over one shoulder and a sack that clinks, the
vagabond has decided grave-robber is the costume that suits him, and he may
not be entirely in costume. He is looking for victims, as always; tonight he
2431: A happy drunk in crooked devil horns wanders about, singing about Moria.
The horns are on a headband that has slid over one ear, the tail is
dragging, and the song is the same song about Moria that he sings every
other night of the year, but louder. He is having a wonderful Hallows End
and would like you to have one too.
2432: A beggar holds out a hollowed pumpkin, asking for a few coins or a sweet.
The beggar has carved his begging bowl out of a pumpkin for the night, and
it works: children who would never give him a coin drop candy in it without
a thought, and he is doing better than he has all year. He asks you for a
2433: A black cat hisses at you from the shadows, tail lashing.
A black alley cat, half mad and more than a little mean, and tonight of all
nights entirely sure of its own importance. Somebody has tied an orange
ribbon round its neck. It is not pleased about that either.
2434: A small trick-or-treater in a bedsheet demands candy, or else.
The sheet has eyeholes cut too far apart, so the trick-or-treater keeps
tilting its head to see out of one at a time. It shoves a sack at you and
demands candy, or else, and seems unclear on what the else would be. It is
2435: A janitor in zombie greasepaint shambles about, sweeping up candy wrappers.
Grey greasepaint, a torn uniform and a convincing shamble, undone slightly
by the broom and dustpan and the way he mutters about the mess. The janitor
is cleaning up after the fair as he cleans up after everything, and has gone
as a zombie because, he says, it is how he feels.
2436: A witch's broom hovers at knee height, bristles twitching to be ridden.
A gnarled but straight stick with straw bound to one end, hanging in the air
at exactly the height of a cute little pony's back and quivering slightly.
It will take you places, the stable-hand swears, and it is much easier to
2437: A pack mule painted in white bones stands patiently under its load.
Somebody with time and a pot of whitewash has painted a full skeleton on
this weary pack mule, ribs, skull and all, and the mule has borne it as it
bears everything. It is a horrendous sight, in a mild sort of way.
2438: A handsome gelding draped in a white sheet, eyeholes and all, stands here.
A handsome gelding wearing a bedsheet with two eyeholes, through which it
regards you with enormous patience. The sheet is tied under its belly with a
bootlace. It is, the stables insist, a ghost horse.
2439: A jet black stallion stands here with a jack-o-lantern hung from its saddle.
The stallion needed no costume: jet black from nose to tail, it only needed
the carved pumpkin lantern that swings from its saddle-horn and lights its
eyes orange from below. It stamps once and looks like something out of a
2440: A massive warhorse in barding painted with bones stomps noisily here.
A massive warhorse, bred to carry knights to war, in black barding on which
someone has painted a horse's skeleton in white, ribs across the flanks and
a long skull over its face. It stomps and blows and looks, in the lantern
light, like death's own charger. It would be a formidable mount in battle,
2441: An enormous elephant draped in black bunting swings his trunk here.
The elephant has been dressed for Hallows End in yards of black bunting and
a headdress of paper bats, and he swings his trunk at the children who run
shrieking around his feet. Ridden into battle an elephant is a difficult
steed to stop, and seated on one the rider has the advantage of height and
is next to impossible to dismount, bats or no bats.
4201: A healer of Devota in a witch's hat and wax warts cackles over a cauldron.
Under the pointed hat, the wax warts and the green greasepaint is a disciple
of Devota who runs the haunted temple's healing stall and has thrown herself
into the part. She cackles at everyone. If you dare to, ask her to heal you;
she will do it properly, and only threaten to turn you into a toad.
Type 'heal' to see a listing of spells.
4202: The Grim Reaper stands guard over the city, scythe in hand, looking for
For Hallows End the formless shape that guards the city has taken the oldest
shape of all: a huge black robe and cowl, two red eyes burning beneath the
hood, and an enormous scythe held in one bony hand. It is waiting for the
witching hour to collect its souls and go home, and until then it watches
the square as it always does. The costume is the only thing about it that is

2401: Oak Tree Square on Hallows Eve~
This is the center of the square, dominated by the trunk of the biggest oak
tree you have ever seen: ten feet across and a hundred feet tall. Tonight
every one of its lower boughs is hung with a carved pumpkin, and the lit
pumpkins throw a hundred grinning orange faces across the flagstones. Paper
bats turn slowly on threads among the leaves. High in the branches you can
make out some kind of structure, and the portal carved into the side of the
tree glows a sickly green for the occasion; a staircase leads down into the
mighty trunk. Near the base of the tree a sign has been painted over with a
dripping red BEWARE, which the children of Dresden find hilarious.
2415: You are on a very well made stone road that goes through the center of town,
and tonight it belongs to Hallows End. Orange paper lanterns swing on cords
strung from eave to eave, and the crowd beneath them is thick with masks,
horns and painted faces. To the north the towers of Drakkar's Palace stand
black against the sky; to the east you can hear the market, louder than
usual, and to the west the tall spires of the University of Magic flicker
2416: You are on a very well made stone road that goes through the center of town,
and tonight it belongs to Hallows End. Scarecrows have been propped along
both kerbs, each one dressed in some guardsman's cast-off uniform and given
a pumpkin for a head. One of them keeps turning to watch you, which is
probably a student's joke. The palace towers rise to the north, the market
clatters to the east, and the spires of the University of Magic stand to the
2496: Main Processional, Where the Candles Burn~
You are on a very well made stone road that goes through the center of town,
and tonight it belongs to Hallows End. Hundreds of stubby candles line the
gutters in jars of coloured glass, so the whole road glows red and amber
from below and every face above it is lit from underneath like a
storyteller's. Wax drips and pools between the cobbles. The towers of
Drakkar's Palace are to the north, the sounds of the market to the east, and
the spires of the University of Magic to the west.
2417: Main Processional, Before the Palace Gates~
You are on a very well made stone road that goes through the center of town,
and tonight it belongs to Hallows End. The gates of Drakkar's Palace stand
just to the north, and the guards on them have let the festival get as far
as their helmets: each wears a crown of autumn leaves and looks faintly
embarrassed about it. Two great jack-o-lanterns the size of wine barrels
flank the gateway. East lies the market, west the spires of the University
2427: Main Processional, Below the Temple Steps~
You are on a very well made stone road that goes through the center of town,
and tonight it belongs to Hallows End. To the north the enormous oak fills
the end of the road, a constellation of lit pumpkins in its branches. To the
west broad steps climb to the Temple of Devota, except that tonight the
steps are draped in black cloth and eerie organ music is drifting down them:
the acolytes have turned their temple into a haunted house for the festival.
South leads to the southern gates of the city.
2428: Main Processional, Toward the Mermaids' Bridge~
You are on a very well made stone road that goes through the center of town,
and tonight it belongs to Hallows End. Children run past you in sheets and
masks, clutching bags of candy and shrieking happily at nothing. To the
north the enormous oak glows with its hundred pumpkins; south the road runs
over a bridge toward the southern gates of the city, and someone has tied
black ribbons to every post of its railing.
2430: Main Processional, at the Southern Gates~
You are on a very well made stone road that goes through the center of town,
and tonight it belongs to Hallows End. Just to the north is the Bridge of
the Mermaids, its railing wound with black ribbon, and far beyond it the
enormous oak is a dome of orange light. The southern gates stand to the
south, a little busier than usual with farm carts bringing in pumpkins by
the hundredweight, and the gatekeepers are charging a candy toll of everyone
2487: The Market Plaza has given itself over to the fair. Booths and tents crowd
the flagstones under strings of orange and black bunting, selling toffee
apples, carved turnips, cheap masks, cobweb lace and candles that burn
green. A bobbing-tub stands in the middle of it all, surrounded by wet and
delighted children. People costumed as everything from ghosts to guardsmen
go in and out of the open doorways of the surrounding buildings.
4201: You are at the top of a broad stone stairway looking up at the entrance to
the Temple of Devota, which for one night a year is not peaceful at all.
Black cloth hangs over the white marble, pasteboard gargoyles glare down
from the architrave, and a wheezing organ somewhere inside plays the same
three ominous chords over and over. The plaque above the arched entrance has
been covered by a sign reading ENTER IF YOU DARE, in letters that are meant
to look like blood and look like jam. The acolytes run this every Hallows
End for the orphanage, and they take it very seriously.
4202: You are in a large domed room, and the murals of healers tending the wounded
have been hidden behind yards of grey gauze that stirs in a wind you cannot
feel. From somewhere behind the cloth come whispers, dozens of them, saying
your name, or something very like it. Novices with their mouths to the
gauze, probably, but the hair on your neck is not convinced.
4203: Cobweb hangs from the dome in sheets so thick the murals above are only
shapes. Most of it is spun sugar and cotton, and some of it, in the dark
corners, is not. Fat rubber spiders drop on threads as you pass and are
hauled back up again by giggling acolytes somewhere above.
4204: Rows of skulls line the walls of this domed hall on shelves of black crepe,
each with a candle guttering inside so its eyes and teeth glow. They are
turnips, mostly, carved by the temple's novices, but the carving is very
good and a few of them have been given hair. Something in the back row is
4205: A thousand candles stand on every ledge and flagstone of this domed hall,
and a draught from nowhere keeps making them gutter all at once, so that the
room plunges toward darkness and swims back again. In the dark moments you
are fairly sure the murals move. In the light ones a novice with a bellows
4206: The dome overhead has been draped black so this hall feels twice as high and
far emptier than it is. Every step you take comes back a half-beat late and
a little heavier, as though somebody larger were walking just behind you.
When you stop, so does it. Eventually.
4207: Before you are three steps up to the altar of Devota, Goddess of Peace and
Healing, who tonight is shrouded in black like the rest of her temple. Rows
of candles climb the steps, a fog of dry ice rolls down them around your
ankles, and the organ chords from the entrance are loudest here. For all the
gloom, the room is still the heart of the temple, and travellers still
arrive on these flagstones with a flash of light and a sigh of relief,
4208: The altar is still an enormous piece of white marble under its black cloth,
and the statue of Devota behind it still looks out over her temple with the
same patient smile, though somebody has hung a witch's hat on her. Before
the altar two acolytes in robes and skull paint perform the Sacrifice every
quarter hour: a great deal of shrieking, a wooden dagger and a bladder of
beet juice, and the maiden always gets up for the applause. The stash is
kept here as it always is, whatever the decor.
4209: The pews of the private prayer room have been stacked against one wall to
make space for a dozen coffins, open and shut, borrowed from a sympathetic
undertaker. From inside one of the shut ones comes a slow, patient knocking.
The rack of candles is still here, burning green, and the sense that Devota
herself is watching over you has not entirely gone away, which is a comfort,
because the knocking has just stopped.
4210: The two cots, the wash basin and the towels of the healing room are all
still here, and so are the patients: novices in grey paint and bandages who
moan and reach for you as you pass and beg, in voices they have clearly
practised, for you not to leave them. The one nearest the door has a very
convincing cough and a bag of candy under the blanket.

2442: A searing jack o'lantern flame burns brightly here
This is the result when you play with fire.

2403: A large orange pumpkin, complete with carved face, and glowing candle~
